headline: spot has doubled in a year to a fresh three-year high, and 2027 is now rising faster than next winter - the term discount is narrowing
commentary: UK power spot is 152.00 £/MWh. It has now more than doubled in a year, up 105%, and sits at a fresh three-year high. The drivers are the same two as last week, still running: escalating US-Iran tension, including military strikes and reported attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities, and Qatar's extended LNG force majeure, which keeps replacement cargoes away from Europe through the autumn. What changed in the last day is where the buying is. The back of the curve is now moving faster than the front - since yesterday Oct 26 gas is up 4.1% and Winter 26 up 4.2%, but Summer 27 is up 5.4% and Winter 27 up 4.8%. The cheaper 2027 contracts a longer term depends on are repricing upward faster than the winter that term is meant to dilute. The term argument still holds. Winter 26 at 205.10 p/therm against Summer 27 at 136.25 and Winter 27 at 129.65 is still roughly a third cheaper beyond next winter, so a 24-month starting this October blends the expensive winter with a materially cheaper 2027/28 while a 12-month sits on the winter alone. But that discount is narrowing, not widening. On this curve waiting is costing more than it saves.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Oct 26) is 203.68 p/therm and the winter strip is higher still - Winter 26 at 205.10, Jan 27 at 209.45. The whole board is up again on the same Middle East tension and Qatar LNG force majeure. Summer 27 (136.25) and Winter 27 (129.65) still sit around a third below next winter, but both rose more than the front month today - the far curve is catching up, so the discount a longer term buys is narrowing.
